Class IndicatorBank

java.lang.Object
com.wualabs.qtsurfer.engine.indicators.cache.IndicatorBank
public final class IndicatorBank extends Object
Value series already computed over one dataset, keyed by the math identity that produced them, so a parameter sweep computes each distinct indicator once instead of once per parameter vector (goal sweep-research-engine E6).

The saving is combinatorial rather than constant. A k-dimensional grid re-registers the same ema(20) for every combination of the other axes, so the number of series actually computed falls from the product of the axis sizes to their sum.

It is an optimization and never a correctness surface

Every path through this class fails towards computing live: an indicator that cannot state a signature, one whose recording was disturbed, a full bank, a bank disabled by its own guard. A miss is slow, never wrong.

What it cannot check itself is whether a signature told the truth. An indicator that omits a swept field from its signature would be handed another parameterization's series and corrupt every downstream number silently. The sweep layer therefore runs one vector twice — once recording, once replaying — and compares the resulting trade lists, calling disable(String) when they differ. That guard is mandatory, and this class is written so that disabling it mid-sweep is safe at any moment.

Scope and lifetime

A bank belongs to one sweep over one prepared dataset and is discarded with it. Nothing here identifies the data, so reusing one across datasets would replay the wrong series — the scoping is structural, enforced by the bank being created inside the batch that owns the data.

Threading: the bank is shared by concurrently running vectors and is safe for that. A IndicatorBank.Session is not — it belongs to one run on one thread, which is how the runs are structured.

  • Field Details

    • DEFAULT_MAX_DOUBLES

      public static final long DEFAULT_MAX_DOUBLES
      Default ceiling on retained series data, in doubles — 8M, about 64 MB.

      A bound is needed because the natural size of a sweep is exactly what makes it worth memoizing: a hundred thousand data points times a few hundred distinct indicators is gigabytes if left unbounded. Reaching it denies further recording rather than evicting, since eviction would make a sweep's memoization pattern depend on run interleaving.

    • newSession

      public IndicatorBank.Session newSession()
      One run's view of this bank: it decides per registered indicator whether to replay, record or step aside, and holds the recordings until the run finishes.

      Confined to the run's own thread, as each sweep vector builds its entire mutable world on the thread that executes it.

      Returns:
      a fresh session

    • disable

      public void disable(@NonNull @NonNull String reason)
      Stops all memoization from here on. Already-installed replay indicators keep serving their series — they are as correct as the run that recorded them — but nothing new is replayed or recorded, so every subsequent run computes live.
      Parameters:
      reason - why, for the log and for getDisabledReason()

    • unbank

      public static RTIndicator unbank(RTIndicator indicator)
      The live indicator behind a bank wrapper, marking any recording as unusable.

      Needed wherever a registered indicator is pulled back out and re-registered differently — the series a recorder had started belongs to the old wiring, and the instance handed back has to be one that will actually compute. Both wrappers hold an untouched original for exactly this, so the returned indicator is in its pre-first-tick state.

      Parameters:
      indicator - a registered indicator, banked or not
      Returns:
      the indicator to keep using; the argument itself when it was never banked
